legacy_regressions.coverage: Native tests reconstruct the pre-history persisted shape for queued, waiting and running admissions. Pair identities, runner grant and completion receipt originate in test-daemon operations. They check original-ID continuation, preserved identity, one effect, consumed successful once grant, and duplicate result retrieval without reexecution.
legacy_regressions.boundary: These are disposable localhost test-daemon/state regressions, not execution of an old binary upgrade on production machines.

release.build_behavior: The release command reused the verified native binary. All 29 production/Cargo inputs are byte-identical and the release SHA256 matches the preceding clean release build exactly.
release.new_test_build_safety: The 193 source and native binary were preserved separately. Only the added test was written with a current observed mtime into the established build directory; all 104 source hashes were verified.

existing_actual_two_machine_evidence.reason: Production inputs and native release binary are unchanged.

limits: No deployment was performed by the validation worker; root owns the service upgrade and standing-hand smoke test.
Physical suspend/resume, native desktop UX, sustained operational use and power-loss durability remain separate proof requirements.
Raw exact build paths and commands remain private; DEPENDENCY_TARGET denotes the recorded reused native target directory.
preservation: The 190-test and 193-test artifacts and their results remain preserved, including the rejected cached-release attempt and explicit release-profile cleanup.
